experimental_method: Static vapor-pressure method: differential pressure between a pure-water autoclave and a salt-solution autoclave at the same temperature (oil bath), measured with Bourdon-tube differential gauges and a strain-gauge transducer; molality by weight at room temperature corrected for water in the vapor space, or by sampling and atomic absorption for CaCl2 above 300 C.
uncertainties_stated: Gauges: Bourdon +-0.5 percent of full scale, strain gauge +-0.25 percent of span; systematic calibration/measurement error about 1 to 2 psid; temperature controlled to +-0.2 C (oil bath, thermocouples accurate to +-0.2 C as stated in text); molality accuracy +-2.0 percent (NaCl, KCl) and +-5.0 percent (CaCl2); CaCl2 calculated molalities at 300 C agree within +-0.2 m with measured ones.
quality_remarks: Authors: NaCl rows below 325 C were used as spot checks only and not in their fits; at 350 C NaCl gross discrepancy with Mashovets et al. 1973 (authors suspect any systematic error of their data makes values too low, and note agreement with Lindsay 1980); CaCl2 350 C: literature point at m=5.6 of Zarembo et al. 1980 deviates; authors discarded the literature point, not their own. Gauge responded sluggishly (1-2 h Bourdon, 20-30 min strain gauge). Table is dP (differential vapor pressure) only; absolute brine pressure not tabulated. Non-monotonic as printed: CaCl2 350 C 537.0 (m 6.4) then 528.1 (m 6.5). Replicate molalities within block: CaCl2 325 C m 5.3 (346.2, 357.8) and 6.1 (387.7, 389.2), CaCl2 350 C m 5.5 (456.0, 465.0).
not_extracted_tables: Table 2 (journal p. 680-681): Lietzke-Stoughton and Pitzer parameters fitted to the data (model parameters, with a table of smoothed osmotic coefficients described as available on request)
Table 3: association constants and hydration numbers (model parameters)
